Latin word

flūmen

flūmen, flūminis n.

noun, third declension; in this sense in set phrases

the stream, the current (flowing water); river

In this lexicon

  • current

    the recommended word · classical · Caes. BG 7.58: secundō flūmine, with the current; Caes. BG 7.60: adversō flūmine, against the current; Traupman 203: current (in the sense of “the flow”), flūmen; Traupman 299

  • river

    the recommended word · classical · Traupman 206; Traupman 372

  • Amāzonum flūmen: Amazon

    modern

Examples

  • nōn aliter quam quī adversō vix flūmine lembum rēmigiīs subigit, sī bracchia forte remīsit, atque illum in praeceps prōnō rapit alveus amnī

    just like a man who can barely row his boat against the current: if he happens to slacken his arms, the channel sweeps it headlong downstreamVerg. G. 1.201–203
